import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    correlations = {}
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    X = feats.x
    n_features = X.shape[1]
    
    # Calculate pairwise correlations
    for i in range(n_features):
        for j in range(i+1, n_features):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(X[:,i], X[:,j])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                fid1, fid2 = ids[i], ids[j]
                correlations[(fid1, fid2)] = abs(np.corrcoef(X[:,i], X[:,j])[0,1])
    
    # Remove near-duplicates, keeping first occurrence
    to_remove = set()
    for (f1, f2), corr in correlations.items():
        if f1 in to_remove or f2 in to_remove:
            continue
        to_remove.add(f2)  # Remove second of correlated pair
    
    filtered_ids = [fid for fid in ids if fid not in to_remove]
    filtered_indices = [i for i, fid in enumerate(ids) if fid not in to_remove]
    
    # Compute effect sizes and p-values for remaining features
    X_filtered = X[:, filtered_indices]
    
    # Effect size: difference in means between groups
    effect_sizes = []
    p_values = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        x_col = X_filtered[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        
        # Calculate mean difference
        mean_y1 = np.mean(x_col[y == 1])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(x_col[y == 0])
        effect_size = mean_y1 - mean_y0
        
        # Welch's t-test
        group1 = x_col[y == 1]
        group0 = x_col[y == 0]
        
        if len(group1) > 1 and len(group0) > 1:
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group1, group0, equal_var=False)
            effect_sizes.append(effect_size)
            p_values.append(p_val)
        else:
            effect_sizes.append(0)
            p_values.append(1.0)
    
    # Rank by effect size (absolute value)
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(effect_sizes))[::-1]
    
    # Select top drivers
    drivers = []
    for idx in sorted_indices[:MAX_DRIVERS]:
        if p_values[idx] < 0.05:  # Only include statistically significant
            drivers.append(filtered_ids[idx])
    
    # Select all features for regression (excluding near-duplicates)
    columns = tuple(filtered_ids)
    
    # Check for interaction terms (correlations above threshold)
    products = []
    for (f1, f2), corr in correlations.items():
        if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
            products.append((f1, f2))
    
    # Create weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(filtered_ids):
        if i < len(sorted_indices) and abs(effect_sizes[sorted_indices[i]]) > 0.05:
            loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[sorted_indices[i]]
    
    # Keep model small - limit to 12 terms total
    total_terms = len(columns) + len(products) + len(loadings)
    if total_terms > 12:
        # Reduce to minimal model
        if len(drivers) > 0:
            # Keep only drivers and top 3 columns
            columns = tuple(filtered_ids[:3]) if len(filtered_ids) > 3 else filtered_ids
            products = ()
            # Keep only top 3 loadings
            sorted_loadings = sorted(loadings.items(), key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
            loadings = dict(sorted_loadings[:3])
        else:
            # No drivers, keep minimal model
            columns = tuple(filtered_ids[:3]) if len(filtered_ids) > 3 else filtered_ids
            products = ()
            loadings = {}
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(drivers),
        columns=columns,
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
